html:
The Hoopa Valley Reservation is the homeland of the Hupa people on the lower Trinity River in Humboldt County, north-west California. It was set up in 1864, after years of fighting between settlers and local peoples in the Gold Rush years, and it is the largest Indian reservation in California by area.

Unlike most California peoples, the Hupa were not moved away: the reservation covers the valley where their villages had always stood. It is governed by the Hoopa Valley Tribe, which runs its own forestry and timber business. The White Deerskin and Jump dances, world renewal ceremonies, are still held there. Its neighbours downriver are the Yurok.
